guard_patterns.handling: Require an official public source for the fact.
Retain publication/update date and do not backdate a release.
Retain the observation/reference period separately from publication date.
Retain corrections and revision notices.
Keep provisional and final statistics distinct.
Keep official-statistics-in-development status where stated.
Preserve England, Wales, GB, UK and local-area boundaries.
Preserve territorial, residence, footprint, asset and operational bases.
Do not convert activity counts or energy quantities into observed emissions without a compatible method.
Keep GHG/CO2e and air-pollutant inventories distinct.
Preserve original units and denominators.
Preserve CO2e versus individual gas/pollutant species.
Keep installed stock, lodgements, transactions and annual flows distinct.
Keep asset ratings and operational ratings distinct.
Keep tax revenue/expenditure and physical emissions/activity distinct.
Keep models, factors, estimates and observations distinct.
Retain uncertainty, suppression and coverage limits.
Preserve emissions/removals sign and LULUCF conventions.
Do not create a parcel value without parcel identity, geometry and compatible activity/measurement evidence.
Require all deterministic scope and provenance checks to pass.

packages.title: ONS weekly EPC 16-Jul-2026 vintage QA
facts: ONS lists a weekly Energy Performance Building Certificates dataset edition dated 16 July 2026.
The weekly dataset covers new and existing domestic properties in England and Wales.
The dataset is sourced from the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.
The weekly EPC series is labelled official statistics in development.
An EPC lodgement count is not a direct greenhouse-gas measurement.

packages.title: ONS EPC statistics-in-development status QA
facts: The ONS EPC dataset is described as official statistics in development.
Its release cadence includes weekly editions in July 2026.
Development status must be retained when using the series.
The dataset reports certificate counts rather than parcel fuel-consumption observations.
An EPC record does not by itself establish parcel-level emissions.

packages.title: Q1-2026 EPC local-authority lookup revision QA
facts: MHCLG revised Q1 2026 EPC statistics after identifying a local-authority allocation lookup error.
The revision was published on 19 May 2026.
The issue involved allocating local authorities to postcodes.
The revision mainly affected regional and local-authority allocation rather than national totals.
Pre-revision local-area counts must not be treated as current without the correction notice.

packages.title: Q1 EPC national-versus-local revision boundary QA
facts: MHCLG stated that the Q1 2026 processing issue should not affect national figures.
The affected local-authority live-table content was temporarily removed before revision.
The error could allocate some certificates across England and Wales incorrectly.
National and local-area quality states therefore differ for this revision event.
A local-area correction must not be projected onto parcel emissions.

packages.title: Non-domestic EPC asset-rating QA
facts: In January to March 2026, the England and Wales EPC release reports non-domestic certificate lodgements.
Non-domestic EPCs use energy-performance asset ratings.
The non-domestic scale includes an A+ band in addition to A to G.
Certificate-band distributions are building-energy indicators, not measured GHG inventories.
An asset rating must not be substituted for an operational energy or parcel-emissions value.

packages.title: DEC operational-versus-EPC asset rating QA
facts: The Q1 2026 buildings-certificate release reports Display Energy Certificates separately from EPCs.
Display Energy Certificates use operational ratings.
Non-domestic EPCs use asset ratings.
Operational and asset ratings have different meanings and must remain separate.
Neither rating alone is a direct parcel GHG measurement.

packages.title: New-dwellings Part L 2021 standard QA
facts: MHCLG's new-dwellings energy-efficiency dataset monitors Part L of the Building Regulations in England.
The January to March 2026 edition was added on 6 May 2026.
The statistics estimate new dwellings built to the Part L 2021 Standard.
The data are sourced from lodged Energy Performance Certificates.
Part L compliance status is not a measured parcel GHG value.

packages.title: New-dwelling technology-feature estimate QA
facts: The new-dwellings dataset includes heating-system type.
It includes energy-efficiency characteristics such as heat pumps.
It includes characteristics such as solar photovoltaic panels.
The publication describes these as estimates and official statistics in development.
Technology presence must not be converted directly into observed emissions.

packages.title: Material footprint extraction-versus-GHG QA
facts: ONS material footprint measures domestic and foreign extraction of materials required for UK final use.
It covers goods and services used by households, governments and charities.
Material footprint is a physical-material accounting concept.
It is not the same measure as greenhouse-gas or carbon footprint.
Material quantities must not be reported as CO2e without a separate supported method.

packages.title: Material footprint domestic/import boundary QA
facts: ONS material footprint includes material extraction occurring outside the UK for UK consumption.
The dataset distinguishes geographic origin categories in its tables.
Imported material requirements are not territorial UK extraction.
Material-origin boundaries must be retained when comparing domestic and foreign extraction.
These material-origin categories do not identify parcel emissions.

packages.title: Material-footprint 26-May-2026 header correction QA
facts: ONS corrected three column headings in the material-footprint dataset on 26 May 2026.
The correction changed geographic labels in Tables 1B to 1F.
ONS states that none of the data values changed in that correction.
The correction must be retained as metadata even though numeric values were unchanged.
Superseded column labels should not be reused as current geography definitions.

packages.title: Material-footprint revision-policy QA
facts: ONS provides previous versions of the material-footprint dataset.
ONS distinguishes scheduled revisions from genuine errors.
The current dataset release date is 8 May 2026.
The 26 May 2026 correction followed that scheduled release.
Version provenance must accompany extracted material-footprint values.

packages.title: Environmental-tax revenue versus emissions QA
facts: ONS environmental-tax data report UK government revenue from environmental taxes.
The dataset includes energy, transport and pollution or resource taxes.
The current dataset covers 1997 to 2025 where available.
The release date is 5 June 2026.
Tax revenue is an economic measure and must not be treated as an emissions quantity.

packages.title: Environmental-tax physical-base definition QA
facts: ONS explains that environmental taxes are based on a physical unit with a proven negative environmental impact.
The payment must meet the national-accounts definition of a tax.
The environmental-tax classification therefore describes fiscal revenue.
A tax base can be related to an environmental pressure without measuring the resulting emissions.
Tax values cannot be converted to parcel GHG without separate activity and factor evidence.

packages.title: Environmental Accounts residence-basis GHG QA
facts: ONS UK Environmental Accounts 2026 estimate 478 MtCO2e on a residence basis for 2024.
Residence-basis emissions include UK residents and UK-registered businesses wherever they operate.
This basis differs from territorial emissions.
The environmental-accounts reference year for this headline is 2024.
A national residence-basis total cannot be assigned directly to a parcel.

packages.title: Environmental-protection expenditure versus emissions QA
facts: ONS Environmental Accounts include environmental protection expenditure.
Environmental protection expenditure covers activities whose main purpose is prevention, reduction or elimination of pollution or environmental degradation.
Examples include sewage and solid-waste management.
Expenditure is an economic response measure rather than an emissions measurement.
Spending must not be used as parcel emissions without a supported causal accounting method.

packages.title: DUKES 2026 future-release guard QA
facts: The DUKES announcement was updated on 19 July 2026.
It lists a confirmed release date of 30 July 2026.
On 24 July 2026 that release date is still in the future.
No DUKES 2026 result may be claimed before the release is actually published and verified.
The latest published annual DUKES data remain from the prior edition until the new release appears.

packages.title: DUKES energy supply/demand versus GHG QA
facts: DUKES is the annual DESNZ publication on UK energy statistics.
It covers production, trade and consumption of individual fuels and energy as a whole.
Energy quantities are activity/accounting inputs rather than direct GHG observations.
Energy and emissions can have different sector and boundary classifications.
DUKES energy totals must not be reported as parcel CO2e.

packages.title: Energy Trends reporting-lag QA
facts: DESNZ Total Energy Statistics states that Energy Trends provides quarterly and monthly UK energy data.
Quarterly data are provided a quarter in arrears.
Monthly data are provided two months in arrears.
Publication date therefore differs from the energy reference period.
Reference-period lag must be preserved when linking activity to emissions statistics.

packages.title: Energy Trends revision-triangle QA
facts: DESNZ publishes quarterly total-energy revision triangles.
The Total Energy Statistics collection lists revision information alongside current releases.
Energy statistics can therefore change between vintages.
Revision metadata must be retained before using energy activity in emissions calculations.
An unreconciled energy revision must not be silently propagated to parcel estimates.

packages.title: Electricity generation activity-versus-GHG QA
facts: DESNZ Electricity Statistics provides electricity-sector data and methodology.
The collection was updated on 30 June 2026.
Electricity generation is an energy-activity measure.
Generation quantity is not itself a territorial GHG quantity.
Parcel electricity emissions require compatible consumption/activity evidence and an appropriate factor or measured source.

packages.title: DfT domestic-transport GHG 2024 QA
facts: DfT reports 110.4 MtCO2e from domestic transport in 2024.
The release states this was about 30% of total domestic UK GHG emissions.
The 2024 total was similar to 2023.
The release was published on 14 July 2026.
A national domestic-transport total cannot be assigned directly to a parcel.

packages.title: Transport GHG versus air-pollutant QA
facts: DfT reports greenhouse-gas and air-pollutant indicators separately.
For 2024 it reports domestic transport shares of NOx, PM2.5 and PM10 alongside GHG.
NOx and particulate-matter percentages are not CO2e percentages.
Pollutant species and greenhouse gases use different units and impacts.
Air-pollutant results must not substitute for parcel GHG.

packages.title: DfT domestic-transport boundary QA
facts: The DfT 2024 release describes domestic transport greenhouse-gas emissions.
Domestic transport is a defined national inventory scope.
The release is not a parcel traffic-count dataset.
National modal emissions require separate spatial and activity attribution for local use.
No parcel value is produced from the national percentage alone.

packages.title: NAEI air-pollutant versus GHG inventory QA
facts: NAEI maintains separate air-pollutant and greenhouse-gas inventory areas.
The air-pollutant inventory covers pollutants contributing to local and transboundary air pollution.
The greenhouse-gas inventory covers the direct greenhouse gases under the Paris Agreement.
Inventory category must be preserved when extracting data.
An air-pollutant emission must not be relabelled as CO2e.

packages.title: NAEI 2024 air-pollutant vintage QA
facts: NAEI lists 2026 air-quality inventory products covering emissions through 2024.
The Air Pollutant Emissions Data page was updated on 12 March 2026.
Publication year and emissions reference year are different fields.
Projected air-quality data are listed separately from historical data.
Historical and projected emissions must not be mixed.

packages.title: NOx mass versus CO2e QA
facts: Defra's NOx publication covers UK nitrogen-oxide emissions through 2024.
The release reports NOx as pollutant mass rather than CO2e.
It states NOx emissions decreased between 2023 and 2024.
NOx is an air pollutant inventory quantity, not a greenhouse-gas CO2e total.
NOx mass must never be used as parcel GHG mass.

packages.title: NOx road-transport trend QA
facts: Defra reports that annual road-transport NOx emissions decreased substantially between 2005 and 2024.
The publication attributes part of the long-run change to newer vehicle standards and electric-vehicle uptake.
Trend attribution is national/source-category context.
It does not provide parcel-level traffic or emissions measurement.
National pollutant trends cannot be spatially allocated to a parcel without evidence.

packages.title: LULUCF emissions/removals sign QA
facts: DESNZ publishes a dedicated 2026 web-accessible methodology for mapping LULUCF emissions and removals.
The methodology covers forestry, peatland, cropland, grassland, settlement and other LULUCF categories.
LULUCF includes both emissions and removals.
Emissions and removals must preserve their sign/accounting convention.
A removal must not be converted into a positive emission by formatting or aggregation.

packages.title: LULUCF disaggregation versus parcel measurement QA
facts: The LULUCF methodology describes disaggregation methods for national-inventory estimates.
Mapped/disaggregated inventory outputs can be modelled rather than directly measured at each location.
Spatial allocation does not automatically identify cadastral parcel boundaries.
Modelled land-use estimates must retain their method provenance.
No parcel measurement is claimed without parcel-geometry binding.

packages.title: LULUCF uncertainty/recalculation QA
facts: The 2026 LULUCF mapping methodology includes dedicated uncertainty content.
It also includes recalculation content.
Recalculations can change historical mapped inventory values.
Uncertainty must be retained when using spatially disaggregated LULUCF estimates.
Historical values must not be frozen across inventory revisions without verification.

packages.title: NDRHI Q1-2026 scheme-period QA
facts: Ofgem Non-Domestic RHI Quarterly Report Issue 57 was published on 29 April 2026.
It covers the scheme period from 1 January to 31 March 2026.
The report concerns the Non-Domestic Renewable Heat Incentive.
The reporting period must be kept separate from publication date.
Scheme statistics are not parcel GHG measurements.

packages.title: NDRHI uptake versus direct-emissions QA
facts: Ofgem describes NDRHI as a programme intended to increase renewable and low-carbon heat uptake.
The scheme aims to contribute to reducing carbon emissions.
Scheme uptake is an intervention/activity indicator.
Participation or accredited heat technology does not by itself quantify observed emissions avoided.
Parcel emissions require separate energy/activity and methodological evidence.

packages.title: UK ETS compliance emissions/surrenders QA
facts: The UK ETS Registry published a compliance report on 22 June 2026.
The report covers emissions and UK allowances surrendered for scheme years 2021 to 2025.
Verified/reported emissions and surrendered allowances are distinct fields.
Allowances surrendered must not be treated as a physical emissions measurement without the report's emissions field.
Registry compliance data use installation/operator account boundaries rather than cadastral parcels.

packages.title: UK ETS transaction-list versus emissions QA
facts: The UK ETS Registry publishes transaction lists separately from compliance emissions reports.
The 2026 transaction list was published on 1 May 2026.
Transactions represent movements between registry accounts.
A transaction quantity is not an installation's annual verified emissions.
Registry trading activity must remain separate from parcel emissions.

packages.title: UK ETS ALR/AER 2026 workflow QA
facts: UK ETS installation guidance requires activity-level reporting for relevant sub-installations.
Verified annual emissions reporting is a separate reporting obligation.
From 2026 onwards, ALRs are submitted through a separate standalone METS workflow rather than within the AER workflow.
Installations with free allocation must complete both reporting tasks by the relevant deadline.
Activity-level reports and annual emissions reports must not be conflated.

packages.title: UK ETS verifier-opinion QA
facts: UK ETS installation guidance requires independent verification of relevant reports.
The verifier provides a verification opinion statement.
Verification evidence is part of the compliance workflow.
A verified report remains bounded to the installation/operator reporting scope.
Verification does not automatically establish cadastral parcel attribution.

packages.title: 2026 conversion-factor activity-data QA
facts: DESNZ 2026 conversion factors calculate emissions from activity data.
Examples of activity data include fuel volume, purchased electricity in kWh and distance travelled.
The factors support separate Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 reporting.
A conversion factor is a calculation input rather than a direct parcel sensor measurement.
Missing parcel activity data must not be replaced with a national average without an explicit supported method.

packages.title: 2026 conversion-factor scope-separation QA
facts: DESNZ states that Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 emissions should be calculated and reported separately.
The factor set is updated annually.
Users are directed to review significant changes between editions.
Activity-based conversion factors differ from Defra spend-based multipliers.
Scope and method provenance must be retained in any calculated candidate.

packages.title: Cross-source provenance and parcel guard QA
facts: The reviewed sources use multiple accounting bases including energy activity, building ratings, tax revenue, air pollutants, GHG inventories and registry compliance.
Publication dates and reference periods differ across the sources.
Some sources are provisional, revised or official statistics in development.
Cross-source joins therefore require explicit basis, geography, unit, period and revision checks.
No parcel GHG value is produced in this evidence-only batch.
